title: Rodrigo González de Puebla (London) to Miguel Pérez de Almazán, 21 Apr 1506, in Puebla's First Cipher, AGS Patronato Real leg. 54 doc. 78 (catalogue 617)

transcription.notes: 373 cipher signs and code groups (counted from transcription.txt, clear text excluded). Corrections in the second pass: l. 16 crossed L + o (quien), l. 19 single C, l. 29 'va a' added. ll. 11-13 not re-read.

system.summary: Puebla's First Cipher: a letter substitution with homophones for a, b/v, c, e, i (Tomokiyo's reconstruction of Bergenroth's key no. 6), with one Great Roman Numeral code group (DCCCLXXXVIII, el Rey de Inglaterra); cipher passages set inside clear text.
system.sibling_key: Same First Cipher as targets/puebla1507 (15 Apr 1507, printed in the 1868 Supplement); the code group from the key of targets/puebla1495 and puebla1496 (AGS PTR leg. 52 doc. 33).
system.notes: Sign o serves u and v. One sign (l. 13, in 'ra?on') is not in Tomokiyo's table; a Z with a hook gives z [?].

prior_solution.where: None found in CSP Spain I (April 1506, pp. 385-386), the 1868 Supplement (1506), Fuensalida's Correspondencia (1907), or Tomokiyo; later Spanish editions not checked.

conditions.human_role: WAINUT: the owner set the task (catalogue items 615-617). The work was done by AI language-model agents, and a second agent re-read the cipher on fresh crops with its own decoder. No human reading.

solution.what: PARES show/2208120: 4 images; watermark PTR,LEG,54,78; address to Almazán and endorsement 'del doctor de la puebla ... xxj ... abril 1506' on image 4.
Cipher passages of image 1, ll. 11-29, transcribed in ASCII aliases from 3x crops (transcription.txt).

Tomokiyo's First Cipher table applied: 'por su propio interese que la princesa me escriviese estas cartas que aqui van inclusas', 'los de la señora princesa veo tanbien ataviados que mas no pense ver', 'codicia de algunas personas', 'tesoro de [el Rey de Inglaterra]'.
Word-list cover of the decode: key 0.608; 1000 shuffled keys max 0.292; key on 1000 shuffled texts max 0.262 (decode.py). Alphabet shifts of 1-3 give gibberish.
Second agent re-read ll. 14-20, 24-26 and 29 in its own alias set and decoder: all readings reproduced; corrections at l. 16 (quien), l. 19 (single C), l. 29 (va a).
CSP Spain I April 1506 (BHO, fetched again: nos. 458-460, no Puebla letter); 1868 Supplement 1506; Fuensalida 1907 OCR searched for the distinctive phrases: no earlier reading.

outcome.method_basis: Tomokiyo lists this letter under Puebla's First Cipher and publishes the reconstructed table; applied here, it gives Spanish sentences in ll. 18-29 and fragments in ll. 11-17.
outcome.fraction_read_source: transcription.txt: cipher signs and code groups (373), '?' counted unread; coherent = the tokens of ll. 18-29 (209)
outcome.notes: New as far as the prints checked go. Key state partial: one sign (l. 13) has no value in Tomokiyo's table, and the C-count of the code group was not checked on this letter. Proposed: catalogue 617 stays open as read in part, shelfmark AGS PTR leg. 54 doc. 78.

texts.label: ll. 18-29: the passages that read
texts.summary: De Puebla tells Almazán that people around the Princess of Wales, for their own interest, had her write the letters he encloses; that he sees her household finely dressed beyond expectation; and that the greed of certain persons is such that he doubts even the King of England's treasure would content them. Written as Philip and Juana were about to sail from England; Katharine's own letter of the next day (CSP I no. 459) says her people were all but naked.

reading_review.by: WAINUT (AI language-model agent; checked against the PARES image)
reading_review.note: Four cipher passages read as Spanish sentences; the holes are untranscribed clear text at the passage ends, two unread signs and one doubtful verb ending. The low sentence score comes from those [...] marks and the period spelling.

texts.label: ll. 11-17: fragments
texts.note: Secure words (y de la partida; senora princesa; conviene; bien y acrecentamiento; de el Rey de Inglaterra y del principe; abra quien le [?pedir] que ningun malcontentamiento), but the clear words between them are not read, so no sentences.
